title: Bug: [SmartSwitch] DPU gNMI/gNOI service binds to loopback only after sonic-gnmi#712, breaking NPU proxy connectivity
author: gpunathilell
body:
## Is it platform specific

generic

## Importance or Severity

Critical

## Description of the bug

After [sonic-gnmi#712](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-gnmi/pull/712) was merged, the gNMI/gNOI telemetry service on each DPU in a SmartSwitch now binds exclusively to `127.0.0.1:50052` (loopback), making every DPU unreachable from the NPU's internal gNOI proxy.

**Root cause:** In `gnmi-native.sh`, when no `CERTS` or `X509` entry exists in ConfigDB (which is the DPU's default state), the script falls into the `else` branch and hardcodes:

```bash
TELEMETRY_ARGS+=" --noTLS --bind_address 127.0.0.1"
```

PR #712 added a strict enforcement in `telemetry.go` (`setupFlags`): when `--noTLS` is set, `--bind_address` must be a loopback address (`net.IP.IsLoopback()`). Since `gnmi-native.sh` already supplies `127.0.0.1`, the service starts — but listens only on loopback.

The NPU's `DPUProxy` (`pkg/interceptors/dpuproxy/proxy.go`) dials each DPU directly at `169.254.200.x:{50052,8080}` over the SmartSwitch midplane fabric using insecure gRPC. With the DPU now bound to `127.0.0.1` only, all those dials fail with `connection refused`.

Note: setting `bind_address` in the DPU's `GNMI|gnmi` ConfigDB entry would not help — the script never reads it, and even if it were passed to the binary, `169.254.x.x` would fail the `IsLoopback()` check and prevent the service from starting entirely.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy a SmartSwitch platform running a SONiC image built after sonic-gnmi#712, with no TLS certs configured on the DPUs.
2. From the NPU, verify DPU gNOI connectivity:

```bash
gnoi_client -target 169.254.200.1:50052 -module System -rpc Time
```

3. Repeat for `169.254.200.2`, `169.254.200.3`, `169.254.200.4`. All fail with `connection refused`.
4. On any DPU, confirm the service is listening only on loopback:

```bash
ss -tlnp | grep 50052
# LISTEN  0  128  127.0.0.1:50052  0.0.0.0:*
```

## Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual:** The DPU telemetry service starts with `--noTLS --bind_address 127.0.0.1`, binding only to loopback. The NPU's `DPUProxy` cannot reach `169.254.200.x:50052` or `169.254.200.x:8080`, causing all DPU gNOI operations (reboot, time, file) to fail. 100% reproduction rate.

**Expected:** The DPU gNMI/gNOI service should be reachable from the NPU over the `169.254.200.x` midplane fabric. This network is internal and isolated — not exposed externally.

## Relevant log output

```
ERROR:
  Code: Internal
  Message: failed to connect to DPU2: failed to connect to DPU2 on any port [50052 8080]:
  last error: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error:
  desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 169.254.200.3:8080: connect: connection refused"
```

On the DPU (`ss -tlnp | grep 50052`):
```
LISTEN  0  128  127.0.0.1:50052  0.0.0.0:*  users:(("telemetry",pid=...,fd=...))
```

## Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```
SONiC.master-<commit>
```

## Attach files (if any)

N/A

comments.author: hdwhdw
comments.body:
Update: the issue is reproduced, fixed, and physically validated.

Root cause:

- `sonic-gnmi#712` correctly restricted plaintext `--noTLS` listeners to loopback.
- SmartSwitch NPU-to-DPU proxy traffic uses the DPU's chassis-internal
  `eth0-midplane` IPv4 link-local address, so loopback-only DPU listeners reject
  the proxy connection.

Fix:

- sonic-net/sonic-gnmi#721 adds an explicit
  `--no_tls_link_local_interface` mode. The binary waits for exactly one IPv4
  link-local address on the named interface and binds that concrete address.
  Direct `--noTLS --bind_address` remains loopback-only.
- sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#28564 classifies SmartSwitch DPUs through the
  launchers' existing `sonic-cfggen` render and passes only
  `--noTLS --no_tls_link_local_interface eth0-midplane`.
- The launch scripts do not query Redis directly, parse `ip` output, or poll.

Validation:

- Native arm64 gNMI and telemetry container build passed.
- On a physical SmartSwitch, both services listened only on the concrete DPU
  midplane address at ports `50052` and `8080`.
- NPU TCP probes, direct gNOI `System.Time`, and the real UDS metadata-routed
  DPUProxy call passed.
- Negative probes confirmed no listener on the DPU management address or
  loopback.
- The DPU was restored to its original images, all DPUs remained reachable,
  the baseline RPC passed, and the testbed was released.

Status:

- All checks pass on sonic-net/sonic-gnmi#721.
- Security, DCO/CLA, file protection, and internal conflict checks pass on
  sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#28564; its broad platform build matrix is still
  running.
- Review has been requested on both PRs.

comments.author: hdwhdw
comments.body:
`--insecure` is approved for every platform, replacing the certificate-free plaintext loopback fallback.

Implementation PRs:
- sonic-net/sonic-gnmi#749: DPU proxy skip-verify TLS
- sonic-net/sonic-host-services#423 and sonic-net/sonic-utilities#4761: direct DPU callers use `-insecure`
- sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#28915: both launchers use `--insecure` and pin the source commits

sonic-net/sonic-gnmi#721 and sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#28564 are closed as superseded.

Focused tests pass. CI and physical SmartSwitch validation remain.

comments.author: hdwhdw
comments.body:
Physical qualification found and corrected one integration gap: when existing ConfigDB had `client_auth=true`, the ephemeral TLS server still required a client certificate that callers cannot provision.

sonic-buildimage#28915 now forces `--allow_no_client_auth` only for the certificate-free `--insecure` fallback. Configured certificate/mTLS paths remain unchanged. On the candidate DPU, the corrected launcher ran with `--insecure --allow_no_client_auth`, and direct NPU-to-DPU TLS `System.Time` passed. Rebuilt-image and full proxy/caller validation continue.

comments.author: hdwhdw
comments.body:
Physical qualification also found that both direct reboot callers trusted only configured `gnmi_port=8080`, while the BF3 candidate exposed native gNMI on `50052`. DPUProxy already retries common ports.

sonic-host-services#423 and sonic-utilities#4761 now mirror that robustness safely: probe configured/8080/50052 with bounded, side-effect-free `System.Time`, then send `Reboot` exactly once on the selected port and poll status there. sonic-buildimage#28915 pins these updated heads.

The testbed was restored to exact baseline images, all four DPUs were Online, temporary artifacts were removed, and the lock was released READY. Final rebuilt-image validation is pending.

linkedPullRequests.title: [gNMI] Encrypt certificate-free DPU fallback
linkedPullRequests.author: hdwhdw
linkedPullRequests.body:
## Why

SmartSwitch DPUs need TLS-encrypted native gNMI on the isolated midplane when no usable server certificate/key pair is configured. Other platforms must retain their existing launch behavior.

Fixes #28540. Source-pointer integration is separate in #28931.

Microsoft ADO (number only): 39179389

## What

- Detect a SmartSwitch DPU when `DEVICE_METADATA|localhost` has `type=SmartSwitchDPU` or `switch_type=dpu`.
- On a DPU only, use ephemeral self-signed TLS when no usable server certificate/key pair is configured.
- Add `--allow_no_client_auth` for that DPU fallback so DPUProxy can connect without a client certificate.
- Preserve configured-certificate, explicit application-authentication, and UDS-only native gNMI behavior.
- Preserve non-DPU transport selection, including the existing plaintext loopback fallback.
- Quote JSON/filter input and normalize top-level JSON `null` to empty so a missing `certs` object does not hide a valid legacy `x509` configuration.

### Examples

| Device metadata | Certificate configuration | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type=SmartSwitchDPU` | none | `--insecure --allow_no_client_auth` |
| `switch_type=dpu` | `server_crt=null`, key configured | ignore the incomplete pair and use the same DPU ephemeral-TLS fallback |
| DPU | complete certificate/key and CA | preserve configured TLS/mTLS arguments |
| non-DPU | none | preserve `--noTLS --bind_address 127.0.0.1` |
| non-DPU | `certs=null`, complete legacy `x509` | use the configured `x509` certificate/key instead of treating `"null"` as a `certs` object |

## Validation

- `bash -n dockers/docker-sonic-gnmi/gnmi-native.sh` passed.
- A container matrix passed both DPU metadata forms, no certificates, partial/null certificates, configured certificates, legacy `x509` fallback, explicit password authentication, and UDS-only mode.
- The same matrix compared no-cert, partial-cert, and configured-cert non-DPU arguments with master commit `d7ad3d29d`; all matched.
- On an integrated physical DPU0 image, five of five direct TLS `System.Time` calls and one metadata-routed DPUProxy `System.Time` call passed.

## Scope Boundary

- This PR changes only `dockers/docker-sonic-gnmi/gnmi-native.sh`.
- `docker-sonic-telemetry/telemetry.sh` is unchanged. The DPU TLS fallback is the only intentional transport-mode change; general parsing corrections also prevent top-level JSON `null` from being treated as configured data.
- Source-pointer updates are tracked separately.
- The physical image also contained the source changes referenced by #28931; physical evidence validates the integrated DPU TLS path, not this one-file diff in isolation.
